oxygen not included is a special game. it doesn't have enemies, other than territorial critters that are more of an annoyance than a danger, instead it prefers to kill you slowly, making you think your problems aren't gonna affect you until they snowball out of control and you can't prevent them anymore. it's a special game.

The game is just a great time killer! It also helps with learning how to multi-task. Such as knowing which items are more important than others. I believe it is an amazing idea to get this game, along with all of their other games and future products.

CAN THESE LITTLE BLIGHTERS STOP PISSING IN THE WATER TANK?!

also HOLY HELL this game can be hard. It took me nearly 400 bloody hours to finish the game ONCE.
This game is worth it to buy. I played for ten hours and it was fun so far, and it is not a game you can beat easily. I'm on my third try on the the easiest World.
Bought this game when it first came out, launched it and gave up. Well now the year is 2026, I gave it a shot again and now I can't stop.

It's a fun game of 2D space survival that slightly reminds me of sims because the duplicants (characters) act so random and kinda on their own. It gives an amazing sense of other worldlyness with the one amazing twist thats always an adventure to keep up with, oxygen is not included on the planet you land on.

Very satisfying, my computer couldn't handle the game long enough for me to launch into space and I've still had a ton of fun playing through the first 300 or so cycles. On the bright side i have perfected my own layout for the base game and have plenty of save files ready for when i get an upgrade
I have some complaints, but it's only because I've played this game for nearly 5,000 hours. Actual masterpiece of a game.

Oxygen Not Included is a masterpiece of chaotic engineering. It disguises a brutal, deeply complex thermodynamics and plumbing simulator behind a deceptively cute cartoon art style. You start out just trying to dig a toilet, and fifty hours later you’re sweating over gas pressure, automated heat management, and liquid locks to keep your base from suffocating.

The brilliance of the game lies in its cascading problems: every solution you design creates two new, unexpected issues. It’s incredibly rewarding, addictively challenging, and it respects your intelligence. If you love deep, complex management games and don’t mind watching a few early colonies fail spectacularly while you learn the ropes, it is an absolute must-play.

Rating: 9/10 – Brilliant, punishing, and utterly addictive.

An extremely addicting colonist sim game that just keeps getting better with updates. The systems can be daunting to understand or sometimes a bit fiddly (I'm looking at you, liquid flow pipes!), but the art style, challenges and more are all compelling. Each update has added significant improvements, and I'm looking forward to the final update in July!

I want to like this game a lot. I love colony management sims, Rimworld being my favorite of the bunch. However, I just did not enjoy this. It can be incredibly complicated to the point of being just completely unfun. I hate having to look up tutorials on how to run every part of my colony. The tutorials feel incredibly unhelpful, and it's just a bunch of reading if you want to get any real information. Even watching video tutorials I just ended up leaving them confused, and I found myself just restarting colonies over and over. The beginning was the most fun every time, but after I got past the initial set up, I really did feel like everything I did up until that point was wrong since I just kept struggling.

Yes, this is definitely a skill issue, but it's a 30 hour skill issue at this point, so I can't in good conscious recommend it.

Addicting. Incredible. Tons of depth, tons of community content that makes the game so much better.
The game does a poor job of explaining many things, highly recommend outside sources.
Amazing game, great mechanics, lots of ongoing updates and cheap dlcs, community is amazing, lots of different playstyles, definitely worth a play!

This game tickles a spot in my brain, and I cannot tell you what part of the game it is. It's similar to an idle game you can get anywhere, but a sandbox version, where your little people can die. And you also have a lot more responsibility. But it's everything you hope for an idle game to be. I love this game. I haven't even had it for a full 2 weeks yet somehow i have almost 2 full days into it.

The learning curve of this game is pretty steep, It took me about 5 hours of gameplay to figure out how to get my guys to stop dying after a certain point in the game.

That being said, once you get it down, this game is ridiculously fun and addicting. I've only played for 21 hours but those 21 hours went by fast.

Anyways 11/10 I like that it makes me think and that I can really get into it

It can be played however you choose. I enjoy playing management games despite my lack of skill. Play this game at your own pace; it's easy to pick up and contains plenty of activities. You don't even have to play it hastily. 

I highly recommend it.

This is one of the funnest games i have ever played, and i HIGHLY reccomend it and if your thinking of buying it just know that getting started is pretty hard but once you learn about everything you have alot more fun.

Also i reccomend that you don't look anything up, trust me first figuring out automation and that stuff is hard as heck but once you pull through you feel soooooo good about yourself.

So far no tutorial, very difficult to get a grasp on the game as a whole, not recommended unless you have excess time to devote to researching the game before hand (things like farming, etc are not intuitive).

Very cute game overall, funny "RNG" generation of characters, and some fun events that can happen (steaming your people stuff like that), but the game is early access after all.

Keep workin on it!

Perhaps this is the only game by running which I can disappear for the world around me for tens of hours, however, it cannot do without manuals and I will have to learn quite a few mechanics in order to develop in it. Do you like making things work while trying to make people happy? Do you enjoy watching things fall to bits while others suffer? Either way, this game does it. Sometimes, I just collect all the plants and animals into a giant zoo/garden. Then, I can make a rocket to steal MORE animals and plants. It's delightful.

Good game, runs well, not too demanding. Fun to learn and fun to master, although it can be quite challenging in the beginning.
Although it doesn't really reward exploration of the environment, it is still fun to do so. Will teach you how to be an electrician and plumber without going to college.
Good game overall, I'd give it a solid 8/10.

This game is wonderful. There is a pretty steep learning curve, but that is part of the fun. You will think everything is fine and suddenly realize that all of your dupes only have 2 cycles left before their imminent demise. Learning from failure is the way of the game.
I highly recommend looking at game play videos when you get started to help you figure out the basics.
The difficulties are what makes it so enjoyable, though.
When you apply all of the knowledge you gain from your many, many failures and produce a successful colony it is extremely satisfying.
Another fun aspect off this game is that there are many ways to reach success. The solutions range from obvious to creative which means the replay value is very high.
I would highly recommend that you play this game.

It`s super complicated but it`s also fun. There`s also a lot of guides on the internet that can help you through the game systems. Don`t be discouraged if you have to start your colony over. I think no matter how many hours i spend on this game there`s always gonna be something new to learn

i love this game so much even if its a bit hard for me i dont even mind having to keep restarting after reaching pretty far into the game, trying to make your colony the best you can is so fuckin fun. Each time i restart i do better and better, finding lots of little or big ways to imrove. Also it may be early acces but i already feel like there is a good chunk of quality gameplay.
Really hard, really addictive. 10/10 would recommed to someone who doesnt care to start over about five times because a dupe pissed on the only drinkable water they had

Great game!
Klei makes games that grab a person and keeps their interest, at least they do for me. They really pay attention to their users and communicate the way all game manufactures should.
I highly recommend this game to any one who likes this genre of games.
Kudos to Klei Entertainment
Honestly one of the best games I've ever played. Devs are always adding updates as well :) 10/10

I enjoy this game a lot. You can play this game casually and have a few deaths and go all sciency and make the most efficient base. The characters are super adorable, so just looking at them will take a few hours of your normal day stress away. It's a unique game and worth the price!!!!! <3 <3

Very entertaining game! i'd definitely recomend this game to any who are on the fence. my only issue is there are no achievements as of yet. i like trying to find various solutions to the problem of keeping my crew alive and happy
This is by far my favorite resource management / automation game. I do a lot of systems work at my job, and if I could distill all of the fun parts into a game, this would be that game.
It's a game that challenges your planning and engineering skills. There are many ways to support your colony that you will find new ways to play the game.
I wasn't sure if I'd like it. Tried it, liked it, got annoyed with it for it being so complicated, carried on playing it, realised that I liked it again --> repeat cycle.

I'm at 5k hours. Uh.... I think I have a problem? Welcome to a beautifully designed game where they've kept it updated for too long. 

I've gotten to the point I don't even really play modded anymore, as it's not required. Klei's QoL changes have been 10/10 that have taken an already amazing game and made it more accessible/better for everyone by including mods such as disconnection as a base change to the game, making the 'mod' out of date. 

But I can't think of anything better then a modder to be able to go 'Hey, I did that. That's my mod they -installed into the game- for everyone.'

How to play ONI efficiently in 10 simple steps...

Step 1: Create your first colony
Step 2: Get basic electricity and research going
Step 3: Disover the slime biome *facepalm*
Step 4: Die to slimelung!
Step 5: Rinse and repeat...
Step 6: Laugh at your friends on how dumb they are at the game and die at every possible situation. xD
Step 7: Get laughed at by your friends...
Step 8: Die over and over again until you achieve self-sustainability.
Step 9: Die on Friday 13th cycle 666.
Step 10: Go back to MINECRAFT hehe.

I'm sure if you're really into dumping hours into micromanaging then this game is a treat. To me it feels like a job, and once I saw the research panel and all that extra stuff I'd need to keep digging and building and micromanaging, I just thought I should be getting paid for that stuff. Not for me but you guys who wanna work in local government have at it.

Great game if you enjoy difficult and complex games that need an insane amount of planing and micromanagement. (Don't let the beautiful & cute Artstyle fool you, the game is brutal)

The leaerning curve is very steep and is not the game for you if you just want to build something and relax, if you don't exactly know what you're doing the whole colony goes south real quick.

I loved the game at first but lost interest in the game after ~80 hours of losing over and over, at some point it becomes incredibly hard to keep your colonists happy/healthy/alive it's just no fun anymore (for me).

tldr
If you love to micromanage and plan the crap out of games, go for it you won't regret it.
If you just want to buildand relax, stay away.

Edit:

Just to be clear, "Oxygen not included" is not a bad game, in fact it's a great game! I gave it a "thumps down" because i wouldn't recommend it for the vast majority of players.

I always looked at this game and it's cartoonish graphics and vertical maps and thought to myself there is no way I would enjoy this game.

100 hours later and still on my first colony, a significant portion of my map is a cemetery dedicated to the scores of duplicants that gave their life so I could learn the basics of the game.

I honestly can't stop playing this.

I am addicted to this game. There is so much stuff to learn and so much strategy involved including base design, how you assign your people and their skill, and so much more. I haven't even done a lot of stuff in the game and I have logged 28 hours. Overall, this game is amazing and I highly recommend that you get it.

Unfortunately, this game is completely UNoptimized. I did put in some hours (1400+). I even watched videos on YT. People were complaining, that only 5% of players ever launched a rocket. Well... guess why that might be. Could it be, because by cycle 800 the game just becomes entirely unplayable and it starts just killing your PC? Maybe, because by cycle 900 I couldn't even let the damned game run so that volcano would make a little more gold, but instead it just kept freezing up?

Long story short: There's a reason only a few players evere reached the "end game". And that is, that most people just will not be able to finish any run, due to our PCs not being 16Qbit-quantum computers. YOU SIMPLY CAN NOT FINISH THE GAME WITH MODERN HARDWARE!

Unfortunately, after so many hours, this game never let me win. It just started freezing up and crashing....
Fun game to play and unwind while listening to a podcast or just the chiptune music. I love the game, been playing for YEARS.

I love the ability to change what effects are in place on your duplicants, you can make this as easy or hard on yourself as you like! The different worlds are interesting challenges, the art style is cute and extremely clear - there's a lot on screen but it doesn't overwhelm. It's paced nicely, with the option to go slowly if stuff's going on too.

This game is beautiful, the devs put a lot of artistic work into every detail. In fact it is so beautiful that I often find myself staring at the tiny moving parts of my many machines, while my facility runs dry of oxygen because I left no airlocks between the main base and a nearby nautral gas geyser. This game involves a lot of oh shit moments when your electrolyser isn't pupming because the pressurer is too high and all your oxygen is on the other side of the base and it takes 5 airlocks to get there. Once you start getting the hand of things, you start to not make as many mistakes, and start planning the infrastructure and layout of your vital operations before making too many building mistakes. It takes a bit to understand the workings of everything, but when you do it gets a lot more interesting.

My advice for anyone starting. Screw up alot. You don't learn anything from not letting everyone die a few times.

8/10 even though it is still in early access, the devs are really promising and I have no doubt that they will continue to update this game, long after the release of their next game.

Well, it is different from other games. And maybe that is why it is interesting to play it. Some things like plastic is not easy to get. It is not like you proceed in linear manner, discover this, and you will get this... Not exactly. Even you have discovered the technology, the resources are not easy to find. And there are a lot of playing strategies you can choose from... if you even knew what they are at the begining. :) If you like strategy, simulation and survival games - it is all in here :)

The ability to plan ahead and build, combined with slowly expanding the map keeps the game feeling fresh as time goes on. It can feel like information overload if you start researching guides right away, since many assume a base understanding of the game, but slowly figuring it out, and focusing on one aspect as the game intended makes it a lot easier.

Incredibly cute animations, it doesn't take long to adore the Duplicants thanks to the personality given to them. I was crushed the first time I killed a Duplicant. And every time after. Thank goodness for being able to save whenever.
Owned the game for about 6 years, cant play it anymore, cant have my money back, cant download an old version. Steam as a resource has been trash since they took away half my library.

I think it's a very fun survival game. I thoroughly enjoy how everything builds upon itself. I think the situations and things to find are great! Klei has done a terrific job with the various systems. There is a lot to discover, a lot to mess up and MOST of the time, it's something I didn't anticipate happening. Other times it's just frustrating AI or requirements that aren't clearly spelled out.

Having said that, here are my gripes:
I think rockets are bolted on at the end and don't really fit the theme. Once you can use them, there's very little else to do but tediously manage your rockets. I liked finding stuff, but when rockets take a dozen cycles to set up, a dozen or more to launch/return... it gets old fast.
Finish the Encyclopedia! I really hate having to look up stuff on the internet because the encyclopedia is either actually missing or incomplete. It would be a much better experience if everything was in the encyclopedia. Such as all inputs/outputs of a building. All relevant information about the critter AND its morphs. Some good encylopedia info on the jobs and the job buildings would be great. This game has SO MUCH available to you, but half of it is never ever mentioned.

Well, 57 hours in and wow. Pretty much my highlight of my last few days this game. The details that have gone into it is amazing. I have admit iv have been on youtube quite a lot to look a few things up, especially how to remove germs from water. This has become my first game to play when i have free time. Yes i would recommend to friends. Love it!.

Super interesting and original game, with a lot of potential.
Unfortunately, they are some issues that cause headache right now.

But you tell me, the game is still in Early Access. True, but when you you start to create Adds-on for your game, your Early-Access time is gone.

I like :
- The originality.
- The physic gaz model.
- Fun character reaction.
- All the machinerie your can build. And you can build a lot of them.

To Improve :
- It is hard to understand how to use some items at first.
- I still struggle a lot with the ventilation and the canister machine.
- Ressource deplete fast. You have to push your research to the limit to stay alive.
- As the colony grow, it is harder and harder to maintain the place livable.
- Food is hard to get, water get polluted, air get polluted, heat kill your plants... life is hard.

Please, make the game just a little more forgiving...

This game encourages you to be creative and actively challenges you think well into the future. The moments of peace are, as the cliche goes, "the calm before the storm".

The sound design and audio in general is some of the best I have heard in any game. Almost everything makes a unique sound.

The main problem with it is the game breaking lag after 1500 cycles or having more than 30 dupes at the same time. Jet-suits, too many objects on the ground, etc. anything that creates a new pathway will all bring the game to a slow grind. That said, I have nearly a thousand hours logged and completed every achievement because of how addicting this game is up until it becomes unplayable.

Many of the most complicated designs are not even feasible in survival mode, depending on the resources you have available.

This game does not hold your hand, you will fail, over and over, learning something new with each failed colony, becoming increasingly utilitarian with every attempt. Sometimes you learn that you made a mistake 100 cycles ago that will mean the end to your colony. The learning curve is there, it took me 300hrs to get a base that survived to get into space.

Would be 10/10 but the lag can make the game unplayable. 8/10

Still one of my favorite games.

the learning curve is a little bit steep as it involves a smidge of real world science unlike frostpunk, AOE, civ6 and stellaris. if you neglect your food production, oxygen production or your materials use, you will loose your colonist/dupes. but when you do get it? past the middle stage hump? it will suck you in. but i suggest you install some mods as this game pacing is rather slow. been playing this while working only after i have established food and oxygen sustainability. if you are getting this, also get the DLC, it adds a few more problems to solve and its rather fun.

regarding your pc spec; game play starts to a crawl when you reach end game as your CPU struggles to simulate every minute detail of thermal mass that is changing, every cell of gas, moving liquids in your pipes, the movement of dupes/colonist in the entire map your CPU will chug. the game does not care if you have the latest and greatest GPU in the market, all it cares is about your single core boost. when i say chug i mean chug from 200fps to 15-30fps

TLDR: math tickles your brain? you'll love this. but you need good single core boost cpu. 5ghz the better.

This is a game that i feel i can always return to. The gameplay, music and animation is so fun. I usually play it on easy because i like to play it relaxed but even there its still not safe and boring. Love that the DLC fits better with my shorter game bursts and keeps me playing with shorter term goals.
This game is on my short list of all time favorites

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (96%): players mostly praise the game's challenge and its gameplay.
Bugs and crashes are the most common complaint, though their share has fallen in recent reviews.

details.text: Recent reviews are a little less positive at 92%, but far fewer now complain about bugs and crashes, which matters for anyone buying today.
New players are much less positive than long-time ones, 69% against 97%, so early impressions can differ from later ones.
